p.title: Meera and the river
p.challenge: Put Meera's story in order. What gives her the courage to act?
panels: Every morning Meera watches children walk to school with their bags.
"I want to read books too," she whispers.
The river splashes: "Go on, little one. Even I keep moving forward."
Meera asks her father if she can join the village school.

p.title: Try again: the kite poem
p.challenge: Put the lines of the poem in order. Use the rhymes two/do, tail/fail and say/way as clues

I sighed, "Now what am I to do?"
I tied the string, I fixed the tail,
I tried again — this time, no fail!
If once you slip, then rise and say,
"I'll try again, a better way."

AMMA: (raising an eyebrow) Is that how we ask?
TINU: (smiling) Amma, may I please have some water?
AMMA: Of course, beta. (She hands him a glass.)

p.title: Into the tunnel
p.challenge: Put Ishaan's adventure in order. Find the problem, the climax and the resolution
panels: The train enters the tunnel and the compartment goes black.
Ishaan grips the window bar; his heart drums fast.
He counts slowly: one, two, three…
At twenty, green and gold light floods in: paddy fields and a river.
"That wasn't scary at all," he grins.

The lights of passing trains go by like flame.
My books stay open, but my thoughts have flown
To mountain roads and towns I've never known.

p.title: Leela saves the fair
p.challenge: Put the story in order. Which leadership qualities does Leela show?
panels: Rain washes out the school fair.
Leela, the class monitor, stays calm and does not panic.
She splits the class into three teams.
The teams move stalls, dry chairs and make new signboards.
By noon the fair is buzzing again.
